"Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed. I have tremendous respect for Ed and his music, particularly his unique ability to bring people together and spread joy, and I have always been proud to welcome him and his fans to Gillette Stadium.

"I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."

While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he stands by his position.

"I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine. But if those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on."

item.title: High-profile Democrat breaks with party, embraces key pieces of Trump agenda
item.description: Haley Stevens backs Trump administration policies on critical minerals, data centers and public equity stakes in high-growth industries like Intel.
item.content:encoded:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN — Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., threw her support behind three of the Trump administration’s signature economic policies in an interview with Fox News Digital.

Collaboration between ratepayers and data center developers, public stakes in high-growth industries and loan guarantees for critical mineral extraction are all areas where the Michigan congresswoman says the Trump administration is charting the right course. She also pointed to bolstering American manufacturing and deterring the nation’s adversaries from hostage taking as areas where she believes bipartisan collaboration is possible.

"It's not just about taxation," Stevens told Fox News Digital when asked how revenues can be raised to fund healthcare and infrastructure programs. "If federal dollars are used, like what Mr. Elon Musk got from the federal government, so potentially this current administration could be right that ownership stakes should be on the table."

PROGRESSIVE PRAISE FOR TRUMP AS WARREN BACKS PUSH TO CURB DEFENSE CONTRACTOR CEO PAYOUTS

The Trump administration has increasingly pursued direct equity stakes, alongside grants and loans, to steer capital into industries it considers strategically important, such as semiconductors and critical minerals.

For instance, the administration converted $8.9 billion in federal funding into a 9.9% nonvoting stake in Intel, while the Pentagon took a 15% stake in rare-earth producer MP Materials. Both investments have increased in value since the government took them, although those gains are not realized until the shares are sold.

While Stevens thinks stimulating economic growth is part of the equation for balancing the federal balance sheet, she did say that the "wealthiest of the wealthy" should "absolutely" pay more in taxes.

Stevens rose to national prominence during her primary contest against Abdul El-Sayed, who has since become the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan. She cast herself as a more moderate alternative to El-Sayed, who she accused of unfairly singling out Jewish Americans.

DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

Though the primary feud between the two was intense, Stevens endorsed El-Sayed following a narrow primary defeat and signaled that, while she may agree with President Donald Trump on some things, she still sees his broader agenda as dangerous for America.

"I personally think [Republican nominee] Mike Rogers is going to continue to rubber-stamp Donald Trump’s chaotic agenda," she said in an interview after endorsing El-Sayed. "People are going to make a personal and private decision. I am not on the ballot in Michigan."

Likewise, the White House isn't particularly warm towards Stevens.

"It’s rich that Haley Stevens claims to support President Trump’s proven economic agenda after voting against the President over 80 percent of the time in Congress – including on the Great One Big Beautiful Bill, which is the largest working-class tax cut in history," White House spokesman Kush Desai told Fox News Digital.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS BACKS EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY DEFEAT, CALLS SOCIALISM ‘DANGEROUS’

Though Stevens is a loyal Democrat, she says that doesn’t prevent her from working across the aisle, especially on local issues.

For that reason, she threw her support behind the Trump administration’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, a collaborative framework bringing together utilities, data center developers, cooperatives and state governments to keep energy prices down amidst the massive buildout of AI infrastructure.

"I think collaboration is always a promising first step and path forward," Stevens told Fox News Digital when asked about the Ratepayer Protection Pledge. "Before I was in Congress, I had also worked on the bipartisan auto-rescue task force in the Obama administration. I was an Obama appointee, but there were also Bush appointees who stayed on, and there frankly were Republicans who were on the task force. And the reason I'm mentioning the auto task force is that we coordinated at the local level. We coordinated large-scale federal resources."

Later in the interview, Stevens stressed to Fox News Digital that she is "really fired up about critical minerals," arguing that America makes itself vulnerable to China by failing to increase domestic production. She listed loan guarantees for mining firms, a policy currently being carried out by the Trump administration, as something she supports.

WEST VIRGINIA UNIVERSITY RESEARCHERS TURN POLLUTED MINE WATER INTO CRITICAL RARE EARTH MINERALS

The White House did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

Looking forward, Stevens — who has a strong record of bipartisan work — highlighted a few areas she believes are fertile ground for Republicans and Democrats to work together.

"[Rep.] French Hill, who's a Republican from Arkansas and a great congressman, French Hill and I have passed considerable pieces of legislation to stand up to America's enemies, to stand up to our detractors, and that continues to be an area where I believe that we will see more bipartisan collaboration," she told Fox News Digital. "I also feel very strongly and I'm very proud to serve as the bipartisan caucus chair of the manufacturing caucus, our industrial sector, and one of the areas of great success for me in the Congress was, as a midwesterner, working with colleagues on the other side of the aisle to grow our manufacturing economy."

item.title: Small-business owner urges Seattle leaders to act now on public drug use and slow emergency response
item.description: Store owner Matt Humphrey said he called 911 for open-air drug use near his shop and never saw police, as Seattle business leaders demand a public safety plan.
item.content:encoded:
As dozens of Seattle business leaders call on the city to crack down on open-air drug markets, one small-business owner says he has been dealing with the consequences firsthand.

"It's not getting better, it's getting worse despite the statistics," Matt Humphrey, owner of Steele Barber and Steele Salons, told Fox News Digital in an interview Tuesday.

"What I've seen even this past week, I had to call 911 a couple days ago for some open-air drug use right around the corner from one of my shops, and they hijacked a whole shipment of produce from a local restaurant and had it strewn all over, were shooting up and smoking something. I called 911 and never saw the police. We just encounter this really every day or every week, and it's, it's dangerous for our staff, and it's not great for our customers, and I just keep pressing on to, you know, tell everyone we can't move, pick up and root up our businesses and just move them."

INSIDE SEATTLE’S OPEN-AIR DRUG CRISIS AS FENTANYL RAVAGES CITY AND ACTIVISTS BAIL OUT ALLEGED CRIMINALS

Humphrey says public drug use, harassment and slow emergency responses have become recurring problems near his businesses and home.

Humphrey said he was encouraged to see an open letter sent Thursday to Mayor Katie Wilson and the Seattle City Council.

The letter, signed by 38 business leaders in the Seattle area including executives from companies such as Microsoft, Starbucks, Costco, Nordstrom, the Seattle Mariners and Alaska Airlines, requested a 100-day public-safety action plan, more surveillance cameras, increased police staffing and faster response times. It also asked the city to prioritize treatment and shelter while pursuing arrest and prosecution for people who repeatedly refuse help.

"I saw several things in the letter, the open letter to the mayor that were published here locally, that I think are all encouraging," Humphrey said. "It's encouraging to see big companies. I'm just a small company, but it's encouraging to see big companies step forward and, and demand some accountability for what we really are working hard to do in the city, which is provide jobs."

SEATTLE CLEANED UP FOR THE WORLD CUP BUT ONLY WHILE THE WORLD WAS WATCHING, COMMENTATOR SAYS

In a recent statement from Wilson shared by KOMO News following the shooting at the Bite of Seattle festival in July that left three people dead and others injured, Wilson said Seattle Police Department data show shootings and homicides at their lowest in a decade.

"I think it's getting worse," Humphrey said. "I don't think it's getting better, and that's the tough part. It's like when people throw around statistics, that's not what I see, it's not what I see driving around. I see the tent encampments moving around, blocks from my business, from my home. You know, I called 911 last week with a guy, 20 feet from my house, that looked like he was dead. And what I get is bounced around between the 911 operator and the EMS people. And they're like, would you, ‘Are you comfortable talking to this guy to see if he's OK?’ And I'm like, ’No, he could have a weapon.’ We don't know what's going on. This is the kind of stuff that we're living with in the city of Seattle."

Any change, however, would not be effective, according to Humphrey, without the support of the police.

"And employee security for our own employees, and we can't do that if we're not supported by the police," Humphrey said. "So, increased police on the streets, increased response times to when we do call. I think those are all really simple things that we can get in place quicker if the — if the mayor and the city leaders put this into action."

SEATTLE SENIORS BEG CITY FOR HELP AS ‘ABSOLUTE ANARCHY’ ERUPTS OUTSIDE LGBTQ HOUSING COMPLEX

He said he would want to tell Wilson to view the issue as a concerned parent would.

"I would just simply say, 'Gosh, you're a mom, you don't want your kids walking by people with needles laying on the ground or walking into your business," Humphrey said. "If you were getting your hair done in one of my salons and getting harassed by people that are completely out of their minds and high on drugs. I deal with that all the time."

"I know you're a parent," he added. "It's — you just can't get caught up in the cog of process and stuck with all the policy and all the nonsense that's going on. We just have to make the change now. It just — I've been saying this for six years — we just have to make a change, or we're just going to lose the city."

Fox News Digital reached out to Wilson and the Seattle Police Department for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Jemele Hill suggests this NFL team should sign Colin Kaepernick to start right now
item.description: Colin Kaepernick claims he still trains daily and believes he can play in the NFL, while Jemele Hill urged the Atlanta Falcons to sign him.
item.content:encoded:
Colin Kaepernick claims he wakes up every morning and still trains as if he were in the NFL. He reiterated to Jemele Hill at the Black Footwear Forum on Saturday in Detroit, Michigan, that he still believes he can play in the league and is waiting for that opportunity.

Unfortunately, despite our attendance, OutKick could not ask him about his position because he and Hill chose not to take questions from the crowd.

Hill, of course, did not challenge Kaepernick on his statement. Instead, she suggested that she agreed with him, name-dropping the Atlanta Falcons as a team that should consider signing him.

COLIN KAEPERNICK IS STILL UPSET THAT HIS MOM WANTED HIM TO DATE TAYLOR SWIFT, A WHITE WOMAN

Hill referenced Atlanta as a "Black city" and noted that the Falcons were down to Cooper Rush at quarterback for Week 1 following injuries to Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix.

Comments like those from Kaepernick and Hill show how unserious these conversations are.

Rush is not an ideal starting quarterback. But he is at least an active NFL quarterback. He has played every season, mostly due to injuries to starters, since 2021.

In Sunday’s 20-13 loss to the Steelers, Rush went 12-of-22 for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. He is functional.

Colin Kaepernick, after 10 years away, would not be functional. Presumably, no quarterback would be after such a long break.

Hill knows that. However, she also knows the Falcons will not sign Kaepernick, which gives her plausible deniability. At this point, Hill is simply trying to stay relevant on Threads, Bluesky, and racially hysterical message boards on Reddit.

Interestingly, Hill’s suggestion about the Falcons invites mockery of the idea that Kaepernick could play in the NFL at this stage.

Saying Kaepernick could not make an NFL team in 2026 is hardly a knock on him. He turns 39 in November and has not played professional football in 10 years.

A player cannot simply go from not playing football for a decade to playing professionally, regardless of how fit they are.

Yet, because of their conversations, here we are mocking the idea that Kaepernick could.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Further, NFL teams have no reason to give Kaepernick a shot.

The NFL did not pass on Kaepernick simply because he was the face of the kneeling controversy. Teams passed on him because he had become a distraction on a level his play did not justify.

Imagine signing Kaepernick as a backup. With him would come a media circus. In most cases, you can sit or cut a backup, and no one says a word. Do that with Kaepernick, and he and Jemele Hill would likely respond with accusations of racism.

Put bluntly, Kaepernick was not worth the trouble 10 years ago. He certainly is not worth it now.

Perhaps the Falcons can upgrade over Cooper Rush. We do not doubt that. But Kaepernick would not be one of those upgrades.

item.title: TRACE GALLAGHER: Common sense is alive in America. We just need to listen
item.description: "Turns Out They Were Right All Along" shares life lessons from the "Fox News @ Night" host who spent years ignoring great wisdom before embracing it.
item.content:encoded:
During the first-ever Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas last week, there was a lot of talk about the "common sense revolution." It was familiar territory to me because every night on my evening newscast, "Fox News @ Night," we join the common sense revolution — you could say we started the common sense revolution more than four years ago. We like to call it "The Fox News @ Night Common Sense Department."

Common sense gives us a chance to take a deeper and sometimes snarkier take on one of the day’s big topics. The goal of the Common Sense Department is not to accuse Americans of not having common sense, but to remind Americans that we share a great deal of common sense. And when somebody or some group steps outside the boundaries of what we consider societal norms, we love to point out exactly why those boundaries exist. Those boundaries were built over many generations by people whose moral code was instilled through faith, family, friends and fortitude.

When I wrote my new book, "Turns Out They Were Right All Along," I first thought of naming the book "A Trace of Common Sense," a play on my name and the name of my segment. I soon realized that my stories are about more than common sense; my stories are about wisdom that has been gifted, sometimes forced upon me, by a group of amazing people. Some famous, some not, but all of them taught me that hard work and skill are important, while teamwork and luck are also extremely relevant. That means that, at some point, everyone needs to ride on the shoulders of giants — whatever shape or size those giants happen to come in.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The reason the subtitle of my book is "Life Lessons I Learned Eventually" is because it often takes me a while to recognize solid advice. I have a tendency to wave off wisdom, thinking that I’m better off doing it my way. The problem is, my way is often the wrong way, which on second blush has reminded me to accept good wisdom at face value.

So, after spending years ignoring wisdom before finally accepting it, I now spend a great deal of time passing it on — not only in my book but also by mentoring young people, including young television news correspondents. I labor to convince these young people that America is filled with common sense as long as we are occasionally willing to listen to great wisdom, accept great wisdom and use great wisdom to achieve greatness.

item.title: Michael Rapaport cheers Macklemore getting dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour, says 'f--- you'
item.description: Michael Rapaport celebrated Macklemore being kicked off Ed Sheeran's tour on Monday after the singer repeatedly shouted "Free Palestine" from the stage.
item.content:encoded:
Actor Michael Rapaport celebrated singer Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's tour on Monday after Macklemore repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" as his opening act.

"Macklemore don't rap no more, you got kicked off the tour. That's a better verse than anything you've done in your ridiculous career as a non-rapper," Rapaport said in a video on X.

Take a dance class. Take a singing class. Learn how to tinkle the piano. Because when people come out to see a musical performer, you need to perform music, not spread bulls--- lies about a fake genocide, a fake occupation and a fake apartheid. F--- you, OK?"

MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE

"You got plenty of time now. I want you and all your 'Free Palestine' p---- a-- motherf---ers to go back and watch some of these videos from Oct. 7. OK, motherf---er? Macklemore, you non-singing, non-dancing bulls--- artist and the rest of you 'Free Palestine' propaganda-pushing motherf---ers. Oh yeah? L'shana Tova!" Rapaport concluded.

Fox News Digital reached out to Macklemore's representation for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Rapaport previously attacked Macklemore after the rapper appeared in a video giving a speech defending his use of the stage to push political messaging.

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine," Macklemore said in a video shared on social media.

PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS

"No, the — yeah, the career stuff has been a problem," Rapaport said. "There's been an issue. The show's being boycotted. Sucks. It doesn't make anybody comfortable. It doesn't make the club comfortable. It doesn't make the other comedians comfortable."

BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM

He added that he has been verbally attacked and threatened for his stance in New York City.

"Anti-semitic, anti-Jewish stuff," Rapaport said. "That hurts me, it embarrasses me, I don't want any other Jewish people behind me to feel uncomfortable, or scared or hesitant to fight, stand up and be proud, however they do it."

item.title: Mounted police, extra patrols and Kiffin hate: Oxford prepares for Ole Miss-LSU game with extra security
item.description: Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford as LSU head coach prompted unprecedented security measures, with multiple police departments sending crowd-control units.
item.content:encoded:
It’s been building for ten months, and Lane Kiffin’s return to Oxford is finally here.

The former Ole Miss head coach will officially return to town Saturday afternoon as LSU’s head coach, and the city is making sure every security measure is in place.

Usually, this would be just another weekend of SEC football in the South. Parties in the 'Grove,' fans enjoying the tailgate scene, bars overflowing into the streets as supporters keep themselves lubricated during the day and the police department only dealing with a smaller number of problems.

ELLA LANGLEY, DISTRACTIONS AND LANE KIFFIN: PETE GOLDING CALLS OLE MISS-LSU 'HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING'

But, this is obviously not just another game-day in Oxford for the police department.

The built-up frustration over the offseason storylines surrounding Lane Kiffin will finally reach a boiling point before Saturday even arrives.

I don't think folks are underselling the amount of vitriol that will be spewed towards the former Ole Miss head coach when lamenting over the stories created over the past ten months.

Also, this won't be Kiffin's first time back in Oxford since his departure, as he has visited numerous times, even taking in a few yoga classes in the process.

His daughter, Landry, still attends Ole Miss, though most of her time is spent in Baton Rouge with boyfriend Whit Weeks. He just also happens to be LSU's starting linebacker, which I'm sure leads to some interesting conversations at practice between him and Kiffin.

But, this weekend is all about a return to the city that put Lane back on the map, and they are waiting for him.

This was not a process created by the local town hall during a weekly meeting.

The amount of police, state patrol, federal law enforcement and out-of-state help that will be roaming Oxford this weekend should make for a pretty safe day in terms of fan behavior.

One would think, at least.

On Tuesday morning, the Mobile, Alabama, police department confirmed they are sending their crowd-control units to Oxford for the weekend.

"The Mobile Police Department’s Mounted Unit will be in Oxford, MS from Thursday, September 17th – Saturday, September 19th working with local law enforcement during the area’s upcoming event," a spokesperson said in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In addition to the help from Mobile, the City of New Orleans will also be sending its mounted police to the Ole Miss campus this weekend to provide help with crowd control. Also, sources tell OutKick that there will be additional support for the LSU football team, with Louisiana State Patrol sending additional members to Oxford, more than usual for a road game.

You can expect a large amount of security around Lane Kiffin at all times this weekend, while the school will also take measures to not give out where the team is staying on the night before Saturday's showdown.

Look, there is no love lost between LSU and the Rebels.

Lost in the chaos of Lane Kiffin returning is the fact that these two teams have a storied history in the 'Magnolia Bowl', and there is plenty of hatred already instilled between these fans.

But, that doesn’t mean Pete Golding isn’t imploring his fans to use that Southern hospitality at its finest.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"To me, what this place has always been about, why so many people love coming here and respect this place is because of the people who are here and how they make (other fans) feel when they come here. Be there early and be loud," Pete Golding noted.

"But I think at the end of the day, there’s still a respect piece. And this place has always been known to have really, really good people. Let’s not lose that over a game or a person or anything like that."

As for Lane Kiffin, he seemed pretty content with the fact he is playing the villain, which actually takes the attention off his football team, and puts the pressure on Ole Miss.

"I guess there’s real safety issues and stuff, so there’s people that have a plan for that," Kiffin mentioned. "I told the players today, ‘Man, you don’t have anything to worry about as far as, like, attention on you all week and everything. There’s going to be so much attention, hatred, everything on me. You just get to go play. Really, the pressure’s on them."

That's one way to look at it. As for the upcoming weekend in Oxford, you can go ahead and expect one thing:

Chaos.

item.title: 64 House Democrats help Republicans kill Trump impeachment effort
item.description: Al Green forced a Trump impeachment vote that fractured House Democrats, with Hakeem Jeffries and top leaders voting "present" to avoid taking a stand.
item.content:encoded:
Dozens of House Democrats voted to help Republicans quash an effort to impeach President Donald Trump on Tuesday.

Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, forced a vote on impeaching Trump over federal immigration officials' killing of two U.S. citizens earlier this year. The move fractured House Democrats, whose leaders have largely avoided placing an emphasis on trying to oust the president as they work to take back Congress in the November midterms.

The House voted to table the measure in a 232 to 147 vote, a maneuver to get rid of it while avoiding voting on the impeachment resolution itself.

Eighteen House Democrats voted with Republicans to table the resolution, while 46 voted "present." Nearly 150 voted to move forward with a vote on impeaching Trump.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and his top deputies voted "present," avoiding taking a stand on the matter while allowing Republicans to more easily scuttle the resolution.

Jeffries said in a statement that impeachment "traditionally requires a comprehensive investigative process, the collection and review of thousands of documents, an exacting scrutiny of the facts, the examination of dozens of key witnesses, congressional hearings, sustained public organizing and the marshaling of the forces of democracy to build a broad national consensus."

"None of that serious work has been done, with the Republican majority focused solely on rubber-stamping Donald Trump’s extreme agenda," senior House Democratic leaders said. "Accordingly, we will again vote 'present' on the motion to table the impeachment resolution as we continue our fight to make life more affordable for everyday Americans, while committing to holding the crooks accountable using every tool available to us beginning on day one."

But Green railed against Jeffries and other Democrats who did not vote to impeach Trump during his own comments to reporters on Monday.

"They will acknowledge that what the president is doing is impeachable, but they would have us wait. Well, the Constitution doesn't have a wait clause in it," Green said. "I believe that there are some Republicans and Democrats who are considering voting to protect the president. If they're not considering protecting him, that will be the effect of what they will do when they vote to either table or they vote to send this to a committee for further investigation."
